newsitem.title: INDIA: India ICI 97/98 profit seen up 25 percent.
newsitem.headline: India ICI 97/98 profit seen up 25 percent.

text.p: Indian chemicals manufacturer ICI Ltd, riding 20 percent growth in 1996/97 profits, is on course to push its net profit 25 percent higher in 1997/98 (April-March), analysts said on Monday.
The company, a subsidiary of Britain's ICI Plc, on Friday announced net profit of 420.6 million rupees ($11.8 million) in 1996/97, compared to 349.7 million rupees in 1995/96.
Net sales increased to 6.70 billion rupees from 5.82 billion rupees in 1995/96.

"ICI should achieve a sales growth of 16 percent and profit growth of 25 percent, based on its current performance," said a securities analyst, who asked not to be identified, at HSBC Batliwala and Karani Securities Ltd.

"The tax rate will be lower this year as will interest rates. An upturn in the economy and depreciation benefits from a new plant in Thane will all make a positive contribution to the bottom line," he added.

Others agreed. "ICI's restructuring is starting to pay off. The focus on bottom-line growth rather than top-line growth is healthy for the company," said Satish Ramanathan, senior analyst at Daewoo Securities.
He said ICI now needed to enhance its market share in western India, where it lags competitors Asian Paints and Goodlass Nerolac.
The firm's performance reflected buoyant sales growth in its paint, explosives and pharmaceutical businesses, the company said in a statement on Friday.
The volume of explosives sales grew by 30 percent, while that of automobile refinishes more than doubled, the statement added.
On Friday after the announcement of results, ICI shares lost ground on the Bombay Stock Exchange, dropping 7.25 rupees to 165.75.
One analyst said the decline in the share price reflected the absence of any indication of whether ICI Plc's deal to buy Unilever's chemicals business would be mirrored in India.
ICI Ltd's shares had surged 35 rupees on May 7, when ICI Plc announced it was buying Unilever Plc's speciality chemicals business for $8 billion.
ICI shares gained 2.25 rupees on Monday, ending at 168. ($1 = 35.7 rupees)
